title: Shared car scored its position once per flagged driver, inflating 1950s adjusted figures
body:
## Summary
player_match_results split a shared car's current-system points only among the rows f1db flags sharedCar, but f1db flags only the drivers who took a car over, so every shared car scored its position 1.5-2x - and the Python oracle replicated the same reading.

## Description
pipeline/dbt/models/core/player_match_results.sql:5-31 (pre-fix: `where shared_car` in sharers and `/ coalesce(case when r.shared_car then s.n end, 1)`). In f1db the driver who started a shared car reads sharedCar=false (1951 French GP P1: Fagioli false, Fangio true). The oracle `expected_from_raw` in pipeline/tests/test_lane1_e2e.py:74-96 counted sharers the same way, so model and oracle agreed - two implementations of one misreading (registry: test-harness/far-side-oracle). Fixed: a classified position is shared when ANY entry at it is flagged, points split across every driver classified there (as f1db's own awarded points: Fagioli 4 + Fangio 5); new invariant test pipeline/tests/test_lane1_e2e.py:139.

## Flow
- 1951 French GP: Fagioli (unflagged) and Fangio (flagged) both classified P1 in one Alfa Romeo
- sharers counted only Fangio (n=1) -> both drivers scored 25 -> the car scored 50
- mart_era_adjusted.points_per_start_current_system for Fangio 17.118 (true 16.000) - the M1 headline figure
- fix: sharers groups every started entry at a position having bool_or(shared_car); oracle reads the flag the same way

## Expected impact
Every era-adjusted video and co-pilot answer about the 1950s: Fangio 17.118 -> 16.000 pts/start, Ascari 14.290 -> 13.645 (rank 2 -> 4), Farina 13.273 -> 12.652, Moss 9.242 -> 8.720. The recorded M1 LLM replay fixture cites these facts; it is already invalidated by the v2026.16.0 snapshot (see the replay-fixture card), so one re-record covers both.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a shared car's points sum to its position's points
Before: fixture: 22 shared (race, position) groups over-scored (1951 FRA P1 = 50.0); real warehouse copy: 85 shared groups with an unflagged starter
After: 0 groups off on the fixture and on a scratch build of the real v2026.16.0 snapshot (57/57 dbt tests pass); Fangio 16.000
Method: gate - new invariant test red (22) then green; real-data scratch build re-measured
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
pipeline/dbt/models/core/player_match_results.sql:8-12 sharers now `where started and position_number is not null ... having bool_or(shared_car)`
fixture CSV race 11: `11 1 luigi-fagioli false 4.0` / `11 1 juan-manuel-fangio true 5.0`
real copy probe: Fangio old 873.0 pts / 51 starts = 17.118 -> 816.0 = 16.000

title: Titles counted the leader of a season still in progress
body:
## Summary
mart_era_adjusted counted a World Championship for every season with championship_position = 1, so the 2026 leader (season 16 of 23 rounds) was credited a title he has not won.

## Description
pipeline/dbt/models/marts/mart_era_adjusted.sql:15 (pre-fix `count(*) filter (where championship_position = 1)`). f1db's seasons_driver_standings carries championshipWon (false for the in-progress leader). The in-progress season is a state nobody designed for: it renders exactly like a finished one. Fixed: staging exposes championship_won (pipeline/dbt/models/staging/f1db/stg_f1db__season_driver_standings.sql:7), core carries it (pipeline/dbt/models/core/player_season_stats.sql:31), the mart counts it; llm copy for titles and championship_position ("the CURRENT position" for the season in progress) says so.

## Flow
- co-pilot queries llm.f1_driver_era_adjusted titles for kimi-antonelli
- mart counted 2026 position 1 -> titles = 1
- f1db total_championship_wins = 0
- fix: titles = count(*) filter (where championship_won)

## Expected impact
Any video or narration quoting titles mid-season. Could break nothing that reads final seasons (championshipWon is true for all 76 completed seasons).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - titles equal f1db's championships won
Before: real copy: 1 driver titles 1 vs f1db 0; fixture oracle test red {'kimi-antonelli': (1, 0)}
After: 0 mismatches vs f1db total_championship_wins on the real scratch build; oracle test green
Method: gate - far-side oracle on the fixture CSV (championshipWon), red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
pipeline/dbt/models/marts/mart_era_adjusted.sql:15
real parquet: (2026, 'kimi-antonelli', 1, False); 76 championshipWon over 77 seasons

title: Season points_awarded omitted Sprint points while documented as 'as awarded'
body:
## Summary
player_season_stats.points_awarded is Grand Prix only, but llm.f1_driver_seasons called it 'points as awarded that season' and disagreed with f1_season_standings_by_round (GP + Sprint) in every Sprint-era season.

## Description
pipeline/dbt/models/core/player_season_stats.sql:17 sums GP entries only; the sprint results never reached season grain. Registry: data-access/read-models-and-projections - a projected number carries its predicate. Fixed: core and llm.f1_driver_seasons carry sprint_points (pipeline/dbt/models/core/player_season_stats.sql:22-29, pipeline/dbt/models/llm/f1_driver_seasons.sql:4); the points_awarded copy on f1_driver_seasons, f1_driver_era_adjusted (+ rank_raw) and f1_constructor_seasons now says Grand Prix only (constructor: Indianapolis 500 included - 128 constructor-season rows have races_started 0 and Indy points). Career figures deliberately unchanged (see the career-sprint card).

## Flow
- co-pilot quotes Verstappen 2024 points from f1_driver_seasons
- points_awarded = 399 (GP only) vs official 437
- fix: sprint_points column; points_awarded + sprint_points = championship points

## Expected impact
Season-level videos/narration now get the official total; descriptions stop asserting a predicate the number lacks.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - season points reconcile with official championship points
Before: real copy: 71 driver-seasons 2021-2026 off (954 points missing); fixture 40
After: 0 off (fixture test + real scratch build); negative control (sprint_points zeroed) red
Method: gate - new reconciliation test red then green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: core.data_snapshot read its file outside a declared source; lineage legal with no sources
body:
## Summary
data_snapshot read manifest.json with an ad hoc read_json, so the dbt manifest gave it no parent and meta.model_lineage recorded it ('legal', []); the lineage test named 'every model' checked two.

## Description
DESIGN.md §5.4: every source read declares license_class + source_id. pipeline/statreel_ingest/lineage.py:32 starts a parentless model at 'legal' (fail-open; separate Lane B card). Fixed in the dbt seam: the manifest is the f1db source table snapshot_manifest (pipeline/dbt/models/staging/f1db/_f1db__sources.yml:22, table-level external_location with struct_pack columns so Jinja/str.format leave it alone) and pipeline/dbt/models/core/data_snapshot.sql:9 selects from source(). The test pipeline/tests/test_lane1_e2e.py:202 now checks EVERY model (registry: test-harness/unreached-decisions-pin-nothing - the name is the claim with the most reach).

## Flow
- just transform -> lineage data_snapshot: legal []
- test_lineage_marks_every_model_legal_from_f1db green while 1 model had no licence trail
- fix: declared source, every-model assertion

## Expected impact
Lineage completeness for the publish gate; makes the lineage.py fail-closed change safe to land.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every model's lineage names its licensed source
Before: 1 of 26 models ('legal', []); strengthened test red
After: 0 of 26 on the fixture and on the real scratch build; f1_data_as_of still reads release_tag (v-mini / v2026.16.0)
Method: gate - strengthened test red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
fixture build log: `lineage data_snapshot: legal []`
pipeline/dbt/models/staging/f1db/_f1db__sources.yml:22-24
note: commit body says '0 of 27'; the correct count is 26 models

title: 10 generic tests used deprecated top-level arguments
body:
## Summary
dbt-core 1.12 warned MissingArgumentsPropertyInGenericTestDeprecation for 6 unique-combination and 4 relationships tests whose arguments sat at the top level.

## Description
pipeline/dbt/models/core/_core__models.yml, pipeline/dbt/models/staging/f1db/_f1db__models.yml, pipeline/dbt/models/llm/_llm__models.yml. The deprecation is slated to become an error; dbt parse is the M0 DoD gate. Fixed: arguments nested under `arguments:`; a no-warehouse guard pipeline/tests/test_dbt_project.py reads the YAML (with a self-test that it sees a top-level argument).

## Flow
- dbt parse --no-partial-parse --show-all-deprecations -> 10 occurrences
- fix: nest under arguments
- replay build still runs 57 tests

## Expected impact
A future dbt bump cannot turn dbt parse red on these. No test dropped (57 before and after).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - zero dbt deprecations
Before: 10 deprecation occurrences; guard red (10 sites)
After: 0 deprecation lines; guard green; 57/57 dbt tests on fixture and real scratch build
Method: gate - dbt parse output + new pytest guard red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
dbt parse: `- MissingArgumentsPropertyInGenericTestDeprecation: 10 occurrences`
run_results: [('model','success') 26, ('test','pass') 57] before and after

title: shared_car read false for the driver who started a shared car
body:
## Summary
After the split fix, the starter of a shared car had split points but shared_car = false, so f1_race_results and f1_race_winners contradicted their own copy.

## Description
pipeline/dbt/models/core/player_match_results.sql:26 passed the raw f1db flag through. llm.f1_race_winners documents 'one row per driver who classified first in it (shared_drive = true)'; the 1951 French GP read Fagioli false / Fangio true. Fixed: shared_car = raw flag OR classified at a shared position; the winners oracle reads it the same way; check strengthened from bool_or to bool_and.

## Flow
- co-pilot asks who shared wins
- Fagioli's 1951 win reads shared_drive = false
- fix: shared_car is the car's property

## Expected impact
Narration about shared drives names both drivers consistently.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every driver of a shared car is marked shared
Before: fixture: 1 shared winning car with an unflagged row; real copy: 85 of 186 started entries in shared cars read false
After: 0 (bool_and check green, invariant asserts every driver marked)
Method: gate - strengthened check red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: pipeline/dbt/models/core/player_match_results.sql:26 `r.shared_car or s.n is not null as shared_car`

title: Constructor podium_finishes counted a shared car once per driver
body:
## Summary
llm.f1_constructor_seasons counted podium finishes with count(*) over driver entries, so a car shared by two or three drivers counted two or three podiums.

## Description
pipeline/dbt/models/llm/f1_constructor_seasons.sql:7 (pre-fix count(*)). 1955 Argentine GP: one Ferrari P2 car with three drivers = 3 podiums. Fixed: count distinct (race, position); copy says two team cars count twice and a shared car once; new far-side oracle test pipeline/tests/test_lane1_e2e.py:281.

## Flow
- team-dynasty timeline reads ferrari 1955 podium_finishes
- 9 instead of 5
- fix: count distinct (match_id, position_number)

## Expected impact
Constructor timelines of the 1950s.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - podium finishes count cars
Before: fixture: 4 team-seasons off (ferrari 1955 9 vs 5); real copy: 11 team-seasons over-counted by 19 podiums
After: 0 off (oracle green)
Method: gate - far-side CSV oracle red then green
Result: better
Gate: none

pipeline/dbt/models/llm/f1_constructor_seasons.sql:7

title: No test read driver_race_cumulative points_cum
body:
## Summary
The cumulative far-side oracle checked starts, wins and podiums but never points_cum, the column bar-chart races of career points read.

## Description
pipeline/tests/test_lane1_e2e.py:331-337 compared four columns; points_cum (pipeline/dbt/models/core/driver_race_cumulative.sql:47) was unpinned. Added pipeline/tests/test_lane1_e2e.py:340: each driver's last points_cum equals the CSV oracle's career current-system points (registry: test-harness/negative-control-tests).

- existing suite green

A regression in career-points races is caught before a render.

Method: gate - two negative controls

title: M1 LLM replay fixture cites facts the next transform changes
body:
## Summary
The recorded M1 replay fixture's set_props cites era-adjusted facts that the already-ingested v2026.16.0 snapshot (and the shared-car fix) change, so pnpm e2e replay goes red after the next just transform until the fixture is re-recorded (paid).

## Description
e2e/fixtures/llm/cd4f7d4ade65d0bffd52472c.jsonl cites f1db:driver:<id>:era-adjusted#points_awarded / #points_per_start_current_system / #rank_raw / #rank_adjusted for Fangio, Ascari, Farina, Hamilton, Verstappen, Alonso, Perez. apps/server/src/projects.ts:106-107 verifies every cited figure against the warehouse (untracedFigures), and replay throws ReplayRegressionError when a recorded success now fails. data/raw/f1db/current = 2026-10-04T130259Z (v2026.16.0, round 16). Owner's data/warehouse.duckdb (Sep 30) was NOT rebuilt by this round.

## Flow
- owner runs just transform (listed as a pending owner act in Perfect.md)
- Verstappen points_awarded 3452.5 -> 3477.5, Hamilton 5134.5 -> 5149.5, Alonso 2383 -> 2387; Fangio pps 17.118 -> 16.0, Ascari rank_adjusted 2 -> 4
- replayed set_props fails verification -> ReplayRegressionError -> e2e red
- remedy: re-record the fixture once, after the transform

## Expected impact
The owner learns the re-record is owed before the e2e goes red, and that one re-record covers both the data refresh and this round's fixes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - e2e replay survives the next transform
Before: fixture-cited facts vs v2026.16.0 parquet: 3 of 4 modern drivers' points changed
After: unmeasurable here - needs a paid LLM re-record (operator act)
Method: probe - cited values read from the fixture vs the current snapshot's parquet (read-only); no rung above is reachable without spend
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
e2e fixture: raw_value 3452.5 / 5134.5 / 2383; parquet v2026.16.0: max-verstappen 3477.5, lewis-hamilton 5149.5, fernando-alonso 2387.0
real scratch build: Fangio 16.0 rank 1, Verstappen 13.904 rank 2, Hamilton 13.848 rank 3, Ascari 13.645 rank 4
instrument: operator: just transform, then re-record the M1 LLM fixture (paid) and run pnpm e2e

body:
## Summary
The M1 RAW axis (f1_driver_era_adjusted.points_awarded, rank_raw) is career Grand Prix points; official career totals include Sprint points from 2021.

## Description
pipeline/dbt/models/marts/mart_era_adjusted.sql:16 sums player_season_stats.points_awarded (GP only). The copy now says so (c0dde08), but whether the video's RAW figure should be the official career total is a definition of the product's headline metric. Including Sprints is a one-line change (points_awarded + sprint_points in the mart) plus the M1 fixture re-record.

## Flow
- M1 video shows Verstappen raw points
- GP-only 3477.5 vs official higher by his Sprint points

## Evaluation

Before: real copy: 954 Sprint points missing across 71 driver-seasons 2021-2026
After: unmeasurable until the owner picks the definition

title: lineage.py starts a parentless model at legal (fail-open)
body:
## Summary
compute_lineage starts every model at 'legal' and only raises it from parents, so a model reading a file outside any declared source is legal with no sources instead of unknown.

## Description
pipeline/statreel_ingest/lineage.py:32 `cls, ids = "legal", frozenset()`; its own header says an unproven lineage must never pass a monetized gate (ADR 003 fail closed). core.data_snapshot was exactly this case until 5d3ca05. Out of this round's paths (Ingest context). Fix: a model with no parent (or no source among its ancestors) is ('unknown', []); test_lineage.py case; the replay every-model test (now green) proves no current model regresses.

## Flow
- add a model reading read_csv('...') with no source()
- lineage says legal []
- publish gate passes a monetized render built on it

## Expected impact
Closes the remaining lineage hole; policy-tighten.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - unproven lineage fails closed
Before: parentless model -> ('legal', [])
After: predicted ('unknown', []); all 26 current models stay ('legal', ['f1db'])
Method: simulation - out-of-scope file; instrument named
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: test_lineage.py: parentless model -> unknown; replay test_lineage_marks_every_model_legal_from_f1db stays green

title: Attribution literal copied into 10 llm views with no test binding it to the registry
body:
## Summary
'Data: F1DB (CC BY 4.0)' is hard-coded in 10 llm SQL files and in the source meta; nothing checks it against data/registry/sources.yaml.

## Description
pipeline/dbt/models/llm/*.sql (10 sites), pipeline/dbt/models/staging/f1db/_f1db__sources.yml:9, data/registry/sources.yaml (truth). One test pins one view to a literal (pipeline/tests/test_lane1_e2e.py test_llm_rows_carry_fact_keys_and_attribution). A registry wording change would leave the views stale. Fix: a dbt macro reading the source meta (or a var) used by every view, plus a pytest that every llm view's attribution equals the registry attribution of its lineage sources.

## Flow
- registry attribution edited
- views keep the old string
- videos carry stale attribution

## Expected impact
Attribution drift becomes a red test.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one authority for attribution
Before: 11 copies, 0 tests binding views to the registry
After: predicted 1 authority + a guard; no drift exists today
Method: simulation - no current drift to measure
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: pytest: every llm view attribution == registry attribution for its lineage sources; seed a mismatch red

title: Constructor seasons carry no Sprint points
body:
## Summary
llm.f1_constructor_seasons points_awarded is Grand Prix only (now documented) and has no sprint_points; llm views cannot read staging, so a core team-sprint aggregate is needed.

## Description
pipeline/dbt/models/llm/f1_constructor_seasons.sql reads core.player_match_results (GP). Sprint results with constructor_id exist only in staging (pipeline/dbt/models/staging/f1db/stg_f1db__sprint_race_results.sql); the MCP connection runs with external access disabled, so llm views must read core/marts only. Fix: core model (team, season) sprint points; expose sprint_points; test: per season, sum of team (points_awarded + sprint_points) == sum of driver (points_awarded + sprint_points).

## Flow
- team-dynasty video 2024
- constructor points miss Sprints
- fix: core aggregate + column

## Expected impact
Constructor timelines for 2021+ reach the drivers' total.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - constructor season points include Sprints
Before: 2021-2026 constructor seasons miss every Sprint point (954 driver Sprint points in total)
After: predicted 0 per-season gap between team and driver sums
Method: simulation - M-sized (new core model) beyond this round's build budget
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: per-season parity test team vs driver points incl. sprints

title: SNAPSHOT_ENV is a hand list that must match the env_var names in sources.yml
body:
## Summary
transform.py maps source_id -> env var by hand; dbt sources read env_var('<X>_SNAPSHOT'). A second source added to sources.yml without the map fails at build time with an env_var error rather than at test time.

## Description
pipeline/statreel_ingest/transform.py:20 `SNAPSHOT_ENV = {"f1db": "F1DB_SNAPSHOT"}`; pipeline/dbt/models/staging/f1db/_f1db__sources.yml:10,24 read env_var('F1DB_SNAPSHOT'). Out of this round's paths. Fix: a pytest that every env_var('*_SNAPSHOT') in pipeline/dbt is a value of SNAPSHOT_ENV and every source with external_location has a source_id key in it.

## Flow
- add sources/nba.yml reading env_var('NBA_SNAPSHOT')
- pytest green
- just transform fails mid-build

## Expected impact
Next-source onboarding fails in pytest, not in a transform.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - hand list derived-checked
Before: 1 hand list, 0 tests
After: predicted guard red on a seeded new source
Method: simulation - one source today
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: pytest scanning pipeline/dbt for env_var('*_SNAPSHOT') vs SNAPSHOT_ENV; seed a missing key red
